The robot uses a spring-loaded mechanism actuated by a piezoelectric or shape-memory alloy trigger, with a superhydrophobic surface for environmental resilience. Capillary adhesion is simulated via micro-fiber arrays for controlled landings. The design targets millimeter-scale robots for navigation in constrained or hazardous environments.

parsed.title: Spring-Loaded Micro-Jumper with Piezoelectric Energy Harvesting
parsed.summary: A micro-robotic jumper utilizes a compliant, shape-memory alloy (SMA) spring mechanism actuated by piezoelectric elements to achieve high-efficiency, low-power leaps over rough terrain. The device compresses its spring via stored energy from piezoelectric harvesting during landing, then releases it to launch into the next jump. It operates autonomously with minimal external power, relying on kinetic-to-electric conversion for self-sustained motion. The design is fully legless and wheelless, enabling navigation through complex micro-terrains.

It is intended for applications such as vertical farms, desalination, and urban water distribution networks.
